name: Hawaiʻi Kona lows
headline: Back-to-back lows and upper disturbances reversed the trades.

sections.The trigger: Back-to-back lows and upper disturbances reversed the trades.
sections.What amplified it: Rain almost daily for two weeks, lifted by mountains: 54.92 in at the Haleakala Summit station (UHM) on Maui, 10–24 March 2026, preliminary (NWS Honolulu), a two-week total at one station, not one day and not one storm; at least $1 billion damage from the two back-to-back Kona lows together (DisasterAWARE, preliminary); Hawaii DOT preliminary estimate for road damage about $23 million (a different scope).
sections.Still open: Summary entry: the full deep-dive (day-by-day timeline, steering, how it ended, sources) has not been written yet. It will be added as the log works back through the year.
